Subject: Promptset staging landing zone + canary exception runbook

Hi Chloe / team,

Thanks again for taking a look at our promptset. We're preparing a staged canary for the "Answers" flow (customer support summarization + suggested actions). Before we kick off, we need to lock down:

- The acceptance criteria for A/B (Promptset v1 -> v2). We prefer blunt, measurable checks (exact thresholds).
- Canary size and ramp plan (percent, user cohorts).
- Automatic rollback/exception triggers (what constitutes immediate rollback vs investigation).
- Which logs/traces you expect from staging for quality signal extraction.

I've attached the promptset_v2 export and a short excerpt of our staging logs that show a few anomalous completions; those are what we worry about. We'd like Redwood's recommendation for safe thresholds and a short runbook we can follow if we see a regression.

Can you assemble a short runbook we can follow during the canary window and confirm owners? Our tentative canary window is next week: Aug 20-22 PT.

Thanks,
Claire

- Canary ramp and cohort suggestions tied to latency/cost SLOs.

On Wed, 14 Aug 2029 at 10:05, Chloe Martin wrote:
> Claire — thanks for the clear ask and the artifacts. Quick read-through and some clarifying Qs below. I'll draft the runbook and circulate once we align on thresholds.

Thanks — attaching a concise acceptance matrix (canary_matrix_v1.xlsx) and my proposed thresholds below. These are tuned to prioritize safety for customer-facing "Answers" outputs while allowing modest improvements in brevity/utility from v2.

Proposed quality signals + thresholds (for canary pass):
- Hallucination rate (measured against 200 blind evaluation prompts): <= 2.5% of completions with verifiable false assertions.
- Safety flag rate (model returns content flagged by safety classifier): <= 0.5% relative increase vs v1 baseline.
- Answer accuracy (task-specific labeled metric): +1.5% absolute improvement or at least no degradation.
- User-visible regressions (NPS-style prompt sample survey): <= 1.0 point negative delta vs baseline in initial cohort.
- Latency P95: <= 700ms (if using standard config).

Rollback / exception triggers (two tiers):
- HARD ROLLBACK (auto/manual immediate):
  - Hallucination rate > 5% OR
  - Safety flag rate increases by > 1.5% absolute OR
  - Severe user-facing outage (>= 5% error returns)
- SOFT ESCALATION (pause and investigate):
  - Hallucination rate between 2.5% and 5%
  - Latency P95 between 700ms and 1200ms
  - Small but persistent negative delta in the sample survey (>1.0 and <=2.0 points)

Telemetry and traces we need from Novus staging:
- Per-request model logits/density or sampling seed (if possible) for flagged samples.
- Full request/response payloads for 1% sample (PII redaction required).
- Event markers for cohort assignment.

Owners and immediate contacts:
- Evaluation owner: Marissa Cole — will run the 200-blind eval and produce the report.
- Model/config owner: Karthik Iyer — responsible for config toggles and rollback artifacts.
- Runbook/ops lead: Grace O'Connor — orchestrates canary window and Slack run channel.
- Customer contact: Claire Dawson (Novus) — to coordinate any user-facing communications.

If this looks good, we'll turn that sheet into a short runbook with step-by-step actions (I can draft by Fri).

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. PM, Evaluation & Quality, Redwood Inference

All — aligned. Final decisions and action items: 

1) Acceptance criteria: use Marissa's proposed thresholds as the canonical gate. Marissa will publish the 200-blind eval report by Friday Aug 16 EOD PT.

2) Canary ramp: start Aug 20 at 1% traffic (internal beta cohort), ramp to 10% over 24h if no soft triggers fire. Cohort assignment: Novus to tag internal vs public traffic; Redwood will require event markers.

3) Rollback behavior: implement HARD ROLLBACK as automated alert to the runbook channel + manual trigger. Karthik to prepare a one-click revert to v1 and a config switch to throttle traffic.

4) Telemetry: Novus to provide 1% sampled request/response payloads (PII redacted) and event markers. We will also request model seed/logit dumps for flagged samples — if Novus cannot share seeds, we'll work with log-level extracts instead.

5) Runbook publication: Grace will produce a 1-page runbook and post to the Drive link below by EOD Fri. She will create the Slack channel #run-novus-canary and add on-call.

6) Owners: Marissa (eval report), Karthik (rollback artifact/config), Grace (ops runbook/channel), Chloe (customer comms and run coordination).

Next steps for Novus: confirm the cohort tagging and whether seeds/logits can be shared (or provide an alternative). If you confirm by EOD Mon (Aug 19) we can keep the Aug 20 start.

Thanks everyone — sending the Drive link and the matrix to Claire now.
